- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts revert to lower levels too quickly after high peaks.
- Forecasts are generally too optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually underestimate.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting lag in recognizing downward trends.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent high values, leading to overreaction to short-term spikes.
- Model fails to account for persistent downward momentum in the last 10–15 days of history, leading to underestimation.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 2–5% for the last 5–10 days of the horizon to reflect mean reversion.
- Model should reduce forecast magnitude by 1–3% for each day after the 10th day of the forecast to account for diminishing momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — use a 10-day moving average or smoothed trend for baseline adjustment.
